title: Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill error-correction with decohered resources
authors: Rajendra S. Bhati, T. Bazylewicz, Jarosław K. Korbicz
abstract: Teleportation-based Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) error correction typically assumes a decoherence-free GKP ancilla Bell pair, an idealization that is difficult to reconcile with the ubiquitous environmental decoherence in bosonic systems. Here, we analyze the performance of the GKP protocol subject to pure-dephasing processes, ubiquitous in realistic situations. We show that, under this class of interactions, teleportation, instead of projecting the input onto the GKP subspace, transforms GKP error correction into a correlated Pauli-Gaussian noise process that can accumulate over successive correction rounds. Thus, unlike in previously studied noisy GKP scenarios, the code no longer self-corrects. Moreover, repeated noisy GKP teleportation drives the encoded modes out of the logical subspace, progressively degrading the encoded codewords. We show that the resulting leakage rapidly saturates with the number of correction rounds. Finally, we investigate the implications of our results for motional-oscillator-based GKP error-correction platforms.
summary: This work investigates the performance of GKP error correction when the necessary entangled ancillary resources suffer from environmental decoherence. The authors show that this decoherence transforms the error correction into a correlated noise process that causes the encoded quantum state to leak out of the logical subspace. This finding is critical for designing robust quantum computing architectures based on bosonic modes.
main_problem: The paper analyzes how environmental decoherence affects the Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill (GKP) error-correction protocol, which typically assumes ideal ancillary resources.
main_result: Under pure-dephasing, the GKP protocol degrades into a correlated Pauli-Gaussian noise process, meaning the code fails to self-correct and the encoded state leaks out of the logical subspace over successive rounds.
method: The analysis uses the Quantum Brownian Motion (QBM) model to derive the decoherence factor and the resulting noisy teleportation Kraus operator, quantifying leakage and fidelity degradation.
model_or_system: The system involves bosonic quantum states undergoing GKP error correction, modeled with a system-bath interaction Hamiltonian ($\hat{H}_{int}$) coupling to a bath of harmonic oscillators.
key_observables: Leakage of the encoded state out of the logical subspace ($L_n$), and the Uhlmann fidelity ($F$) of the encoded state.
important_parameters: Decoherence strength ($\gamma$), cutoff frequency ($\omega_c$), and the number of correction rounds ($n$).
main_assumptions: The decoherence is modeled using the QBM framework, focusing on the pure-dephasing limit, and the analysis assumes the ancillary states are subject to environmental noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the accumulation of leakage ($L_n$) versus the number of rounds, and the decay of Uhlmann fidelity and leakage versus dimensionless time for different environmental spectral densities.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem of decoherence in GKP-EC, derives the decoherence factor using QBM, characterizes the resulting noise as correlated Pauli-Gaussian noise, and finally demonstrates the failure of self-correction via leakage accumulation.
why_interesting: It provides a crucial, non-trivial extension to fault-tolerance theory by quantifying how realistic environmental noise fundamentally breaks the self-correcting nature of leading bosonic quantum error-correcting codes.
